result.topic_en: Concluding remarks of the paper: a curve can have several widely different minimal ordinates, so when the calculus yields two curves between points F and H, the times (momenta) for both can be minima even though they differ greatly.

Ceterum satis notum est eandem lineam curvam saepenumero plures applicatas minimas, inter se maxime diversas, contineri posse, dummodo quaelibet applicata minor sit quam sibi proximae utrinque. Hincque etiam intelligitur, quando calculus inter puncta F et H duas exhibet curvas, momenta pro utraque minima esse posse, etiamsi a se invicem plurimum differant.

Mémoires de l'Acad. T. III. 4

items.quote: Ceterum satis notum est eandem lineam curvam saepenumero plures applicatas minimas, inter se maxime diversas, contineri posse, dummodo quaelibet applicata minor sit quam sibi proximae utrinque.
items.english: Moreover it is well known that the same curved line can often contain several minimal ordinates, very different from one another, provided that each such ordinate is smaller than those nearest to it on either side.

items.quote: Hincque etiam intelligitur, quando calculus inter puncta F et H duas exhibet curvas, momenta pro utraque minima esse posse, etiamsi a se invicem plurimum differant.
items.english: And hence it is also understood that, when the calculation exhibits two curves between the points F and H, the times for both can be minima, even though they differ greatly from each other.
